rewrites.title: The Famine Forecast Lost: Cereal Production Is 1.5x Higher Than In 1972
rewrites.closing: The world did not stumble into more food. It quietly grew its way out of the famine era.
rewrites.question: Which shift matters more: school, grain, or land?
says: In 1985, progression to secondary school (%) was 77.8. By 2017, it reached 91.3 — 1.2 times higher. Quietly, school kept moving.
In 1972, cereal production was 1083.7 million metric tons. By 2024, it reached 1644.1 million metric tons — 1.5 times higher.
China leads at 5.2 million square kilometers of farmland, then the United States at 4.2 million, Australia at 3.6 million, Brazil at 2.4 million, and Russia at 2.2 million.

rewrites.title: The Energy Source Nobody Names Is 3.0x Higher Than In 1990
rewrites.hook: Since 1990, one energy source tripled — and it isn't solar or wind.
rewrites.closing: A third of the world's energy now comes from what we once treated as leftovers.
rewrites.question: Which change hits hardest: fuel, power, or waste?
says: In 1990, combustible renewables and waste was 10.2 % of total energy. By 2024, it reached 30.1 % of total energy — 3.0 times higher.
In 1998, access to electricity was 73.2 % of population. By 2024, it reached 91.9 % of population — 1.3 times higher.
In 1972, methane (ch4) emissions from waste was 903.8 Mt CO2e. By 2024, it hit 1,652 Mt CO2e — 1.8 times higher.

rewrites.title: Population Growth Fell 54% Since 1972
rewrites.hook: Population growth was supposed to keep accelerating forever. The data says it didn't.
rewrites.closing: The planet is still growing. It has simply, quietly, hit the brakes.
rewrites.question: Which shift surprised you most: rural, city, or growth?
says: In 1972, rural population was 63.1 % of total population. By 2025, it was 42.2 % of total population — down to 67 percent of that.
In 1972, population in the largest city was 18.2 % of urban population. By 2025, it was 16.2 % of urban population — barely moved.
In 1972, population growth was 2 annual %. By 2025, it was 0.91 annual % — down to 46 percent of that earlier pace.
